newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds close lower after rate decision.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds close lower after rate decision.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed moderately lower on Tuesday, a day after the Bank of Israel announced it was leaving unchanged its key lending rate for June, traders said.
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: -0.01 pct to 105.66
Volume including Makams was 152 million shekels.
"Prices were lower for nearly all bonds, but the declines were not big because the market was expecting a small cut in interest rates anyway," said one trader.
The Bank of Israel announced on Monday that it was holding its key lending rate for June at an annualised 13.9 percent, the level it has been at since the end of February.
"Yields on unlinked bonds are back at the levels they were before they responded to hopes of a cut in interest rates," the trader said.
Makams were trading at 13.8 percent at the end of the day, compared with 13.7 percent on Monday. Yields for unlinked bonds were 14 percent, up from 13.9 percent on Monday.

Prices CPI-linked bonds were lower also because traders were cashing them in in order to move money into the primary market for equities, the trader said. Bank Leumi completed a $150 million offering on Tuesday and a clutch of other issues are scheduled over the next week.
Danny Alt of Nesuah Trading and Investment added that Treasury debt issues made on Monday also contributed to the lower prices.
Prices of the dollar-linked bonds were up slightly following a strengthning of the dollar worldwide, Alt said.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
- Shoshanna Solomon, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
